primaryDirection: AI browser and browser-agent applications plus one bounded developer troubleshooting theme and one deterministic test-data theme.

baseline.source: Prior daily delivery records and docs/seo/keyword-map-2026-10-16.json including additions through 2026-10-27

selectionMethod.webSearch: Current public search and directly opened primary, competitor, and task/problem pages; qualitative topic evidence only.
selectionMethod.competitorGate: At least three topic-relevant public pages were directly opened per candidate; each has an observation date, source-date field when visible, and an attribution/boundary. Reviewer-opened pages are attributed. Official primary docs are listed separately where applicable.
selectionMethod.ownershipGate: Compared against 64 published owners and 130 keyword rows. Exact owner not found for any accepted topic. Nearby broad workflow owners are recorded per topic; added scopes are distinct task/data models rather than keyword variants.
selectionMethod.limits: Public pages show that products, publishers, or developers discuss these tasks. They do not establish BrowserHub query demand, site traffic, ranking likelihood, market adoption, or reproduced performance. Search-result dates are not substituted for actual page dates; inaccessible pages and 404s are excluded from the direct-open gate. No read-count or traffic estimate was invented.

topics.targetQuestion: How can I ask an AI browser to compare trip options while retaining local dates, transfer constraints, displayed fare conditions, sources, and a hard stop before booking?
topics.demandEvidence: Current Google Gemini help lists travel booking as an example task; directly opened travel products describe assembling itineraries, checking route timing and fixed-entry constraints, or planning by real opening hours. These public task signals do not measure search demand.

primarySources.fact: Gemini in Chrome help describes travel accommodation tasks, eligibility and rollout requirements, task review, take-over, personal-data sharing and confirmation safeguards. The page says computer use requires age 18+, US availability, eligibility/opt-in, latest Chrome, English device language, personal AI Pro or Ultra plan, personal Google Account, and is not available in Incognito or iPhone; rollout is gradual.
ChatGPT cloud browser uses its own cloud computer; support varies by site/action and may pause for sign-in, user input or confirmation.

competitorAndProblemPages.observed: Page describes combining flights, stays, reservations and plans from email/messages/AI conversations into one itinerary.
competitorAndProblemPages.boundary: Vendor product claims; page provides no visible publication date and was not independently tested.

competitorAndProblemPages.observed: Page describes checking travel time, last entry, fixed bookings, transfer buffers and day-end location; example flags arrival after a fixed ticket time.
competitorAndProblemPages.boundary: Vendor product claims and illustrative example; no publication date or independent performance test.

competitorAndProblemPages.observed: Page describes date-based daily itineraries organized around opening hours and walking distances.
competitorAndProblemPages.boundary: Vendor product claims; no publication date or independent performance test.

ownership.distinctiveCoverage: Trip-specific normalization of airport-local dates, transfer constraints including airport changes, baggage/fare class, displayed cancellation text as observation, source freshness, and pre-booking stop. It is not a generic source-verification guide or a booking tutorial.

topics.originalGain: A trip comparison worksheet that keeps each value tied to provider URL and observation time, flags hidden overnight/airport-change constraints and unknown totals, and separates public planning from reservation/payment. Cancellation wording is recorded as supplier display, not legal entitlement.
topics.feasibility: Documentation-based guidance with a clearly hypothetical itinerary example. No live travel-site task, booking, price check, product comparison, or travel availability test is claimed.
addedGuardrails: Do not claim Google auto-browse is available to all users or regions.
Qualify current Google age/region/language/account/browser and gradual-rollout requirements.
Treat supplier refund/cancellation text as observed display, not legal advice.
No booking, purchase, credential submission, or actual itinerary research is claimed.
topics.researchNotes: AI Agents for Travel body states Updated 2026-10-21; an earlier search label showed 2026-10-27 and is not used as page publication date. TechRadar exact page date was not independently confirmed in the final source audit; no date-dependent claim relies on it.

topics.targetQuestion: How do I reconcile AI-drafted expense lines against receipts and transaction evidence before a human submits the report?
topics.demandEvidence: Current Microsoft Expense Agent documentation and directly opened Payhawk, Continia, and Simular product/help pages discuss receipt extraction, matching, ambiguity, or review. Microsoft also provides a dummy-data expense sample reviewed independently. These pages establish task/problem evidence, not web-search demand or comparative results.

primarySources.fact: Microsoft describes receipt intake, draft fields, itemization, issue handling, and mandatory user review before report submission; page is marked prerelease/production-ready preview.

primarySources.sourceDateDisplayed: Sample data spans 2026-02-05 through 2026-03-14; exact README publication date not stated.
primarySources.fact: Microsoft sample README (independently reviewed by reviewer_20261028) describes 15 dummy transactions and PDF receipts, with draft creation, attachment, retrieval, and a distinct final submit action.

competitorAndProblemPages.observed: Help describes matching documents to expenses using amount and date, alerts for retrieval failure, and owner-authorized retrieval.
competitorAndProblemPages.boundary: Vendor-specific documented flow, not an independent result.

competitorAndProblemPages.observed: Documentation says to review/correct AI data and submit through the normal expense workflow.
Vendor page describes matching expenses by amount/date/merchant and surfacing missing receipts or ambiguous charges.
competitorAndProblemPages.boundary: Vendor claims, not independently tested; no publication date visible.

ownership.distinctiveCoverage: Reconciliation ledger connecting each draft row to a receipt and card transaction, explicit currency/date/amount/duplicate/itemized-total exception states, and a stop before submission. This is not OCR or form-filling repackaged under a vertical label.

topics.originalGain: A source-to-line reconciliation table and exception protocol covering currency mismatches, identical-but-legitimate duplicate candidates, itemized sums, partial refunds and missing evidence; uncertainty remains explicit. No tax, reimbursement, or accounting-policy decision is made.
topics.feasibility: Document-based explanation with hypothetical amounts; Microsoft provides dummy records for safe learning. No private receipts or expense account were accessed and no report was submitted.
addedGuardrails: No tax, legal, reimbursement or accounting advice.
No private receipt upload or use of employee data in an unapproved service.
No claim that report submission or manager approval occurred.
Separate agent extraction, reviewer correction, submission and approval states.
topics.researchNotes: Microsoft Expense Agent is labeled prerelease/production-ready preview; do not imply general availability. Review of the raw Microsoft sample README was performed by reviewer_20261028, not the executor. No private account or real receipt was used.

topics.targetQuestion: What evidence distinguishes a browser agent's saved draft, submitted application, and employer-confirmed receipt?
topics.intent: Practical job-seeker application tracking / state verification
topics.demandEvidence: Current employer and job-seeker help pages discuss automated applications and status ownership; separate guides and product pages address prepare/review/submit flow. These are public task/problem signals, not measured search volume or outcomes.

primarySources.fact: Google lists job-market research among task examples, but does not say this means automated applications are a supported task. The page warns that Gemini may share personal info with sites and can make mistakes.
Workable job-seeker help directs applicants to contact the hiring company for status and says Workable only handles technical application issues.
Workable employer help describes AI application tools that fill forms, submit across jobs, and may use intermediary addresses that separate candidate communication.

competitorAndProblemPages.sourceDateDisplayed: Published about 4 weeks earlier in search results
competitorAndProblemPages.observed: Recommends distinguish agent versus chatbot, prepare/review, map fields to source, submit and verify, and use a mock form.
competitorAndProblemPages.boundary: Guidance page, not independently verified platform policy.

competitorAndProblemPages.sourceDateDisplayed: Search result published about 2 months earlier
competitorAndProblemPages.observed: Reports claimed bot testing where some tools filled forms but did not complete submission, and warns of platform rules and fake postings.
competitorAndProblemPages.boundary: Publisher-reported testing and claims only; figures not adopted or independently reproduced.

competitorAndProblemPages.observed: Vendor says it records the role, resume version and answers for submitted applications.
competitorAndProblemPages.boundary: Vendor feature claim, not BrowserHub evaluation.

ownership.distinctiveCoverage: Job-specific status record keyed by employer/requisition ID and exact resume/answer revision; explicit draft/saved/submit/confirmation states and employer-side evidence. This does not teach bulk application, form filling, or general status tracking.

topics.originalGain: Evidence model that prevents a UI fill or agent completion sentence from being counted as an employer-received application; demonstrates timeout reconciliation and duplicate-submission avoidance with a hypothetical role ID and material version.
topics.feasibility: Documentation-based process; illustrative data is fictional. No real resume, application portal, job account, submission, recruiter outreach, or result was used.
addedGuardrails: Do not bypass employer/platform rules, CAPTCHAs, access limits or login controls.
Do not promise interviews, hiring outcomes or ATS acceptance.
No actual job submission or outreach.
Google job-market research feature is not described as supported job application automation.

topics.targetQuestion: Why can Playwright dragTo finish without changing a sortable UI, and how can the tester verify the actual drop state?
topics.demandEvidence: Current Playwright documentation, a Chromium/HTML5-sortable issue, a live Stack Overflow question and an independent testing guide discuss drag behavior and failures. This establishes an existing developer problem, not query volume.

primarySources.fact: Current Locator API describes dragTo and supports position/step options; action completion does not assert an application-specific reorder.
dnd-kit is a separate drag-and-drop toolkit; its configured sensor model must be considered rather than assuming native HTML events.

competitorAndProblemPages.observed: One reporter describes html5sortable drag behavior with Playwright 1.57.0 and Chromium and a different outcome with 1.56.1; issue closed as not planned. A maintainer reproduced the behavior on 1.57 but noted that master/next had already worked again; issue closed as not planned.
competitorAndProblemPages.boundary: One dated reproduction, not evidence of a general Playwright regression or universal downgrade fix.

competitorAndProblemPages.sourceDateDisplayed: Search result published about 10 months earlier
competitorAndProblemPages.observed: Distinguishes native HTML drag from pointer-driven framework widgets and discusses timing/reliability.
competitorAndProblemPages.boundary: Third-party testing guidance, not all-library compatibility proof.

competitorAndProblemPages.sourceDateDisplayed: Question asked 2025-04-01; edited 2025-04-05 (page dates checked directly).
competitorAndProblemPages.observed: Question describes sorting a list with Playwright and an answer using movement/location-aware interaction rather than assuming a simple drop.
competitorAndProblemPages.boundary: Individual question/answer, not authoritative API documentation. Do not infer recency from search snippet.

ownership.distinctiveCoverage: Classify native HTML DnD versus pointer/sensor versus canvas; select the matching Playwright gesture and assert destination/order. The synthetic fixture covers only one native HTML5 list, not dnd-kit, JS sortables, canvas, or touch.
ownership.ownerOverlapAssessment: A distinct interaction intent, not a synonym of picker, hover, scrolling, or general trace debugging.

topics.originalGain: A failure decision path tied to event model, explicit final state and a local native HTML fixture. It explains why a resolved action promise is not evidence that the app accepted a drop.
topics.feasibility: Executed once against an isolated synthetic loopback fixture. No real site, production sortable, AI model, or arbitrary widget was tested.
addedGuardrails: No broad claim that a specific Playwright version or browser is broken.
Do not claim the native HTML fixture verifies JS sortable/canvas/touch interactions.
Use final-order assertion rather than action completion only.

topics.targetQuestion: How do I keep a browser-agent UI test deterministic and fail closed when using Playwright route mocks or HAR replay?
topics.demandEvidence: Current Playwright route, mock, and network documentation plus a historical matching issue, a recent missing-request guide, and a separately opened backend HAR guide discuss matching and fallback boundaries. These are problem signals, not measured volume.

primarySources.fact: Playwright mock docs cover routing and HAR; routeFromHAR API docs specify update:true network recording and context-close write, URL/method/POST-body matching, most-matching-headers selection, URL-filter scope, notFound abort default and fallback behavior. Service-worker handling is separately documented.
Playwright documents route handling and service-worker interception boundaries; requests handled by service workers are not intercepted as ordinary page routes/HAR requests.
Current BrowserContext API reference for HAR routing, matching/filtering, update and notFound options.

competitorAndProblemPages.sourceDateDisplayed: Issue from Playwright v1.39 / macOS 14.1 era
competitorAndProblemPages.observed: Issue report discusses recording/replaying state-changing POST requests differently across browser engines.
competitorAndProblemPages.boundary: Historical issue report; not a claim about the current release.

competitorAndProblemPages.observed: Explains missing matches, POST-body changes, route scope, service workers and fail-closed vs fallback tradeoffs.
competitorAndProblemPages.boundary: Third-party guide; current primary API docs control.

competitorAndProblemPages.observed: Backend mocking guide distinguishes replay from update/recording and notes that replay hits do not call upstream.
competitorAndProblemPages.boundary: Third-party Playwright-style Node backend-mocking documentation, not the BrowserContext API; no publication date visible.

ownership.distinctiveCoverage: Test-data isolation and fail-closed behavior for route mocks/HAR, including strict request matching and secret-safe recordings. This is network fixture design, not trace viewing or live connection diagnosis.
ownership.ownerOverlapAssessment: Independent developer problem. The included fixture uses route.fulfill only; it does not demonstrate HAR capture/replay.

topics.originalGain: A practical boundary comparison: route.fulfill supplies a synthetic reply, while upstream/fallback paths can contact a server; default missing-match behavior, service-worker bypass, context scope and HAR credential review are explicit.
topics.feasibility: Local synthetic route was executed once as part of the combined fixture. HAR recording/replay itself remains documentation-only and untested.
addedGuardrails: Do not say route.fulfill tests HAR replay.
Do not say all external or browser background requests are blocked; only configured page requests in the fresh context were guarded, and browser background networking was not audited.
Do not record or publish credentials, cookies, tokens, personal data, or private HAR contents.
HAR update/close behavior and matching details checked in official docs; issue #28167 is historical only.
topics.researchNotes: The Microsoft Learn API-mocking sample URL initially considered returned 404 and was removed; it is not counted as opened evidence. The third task/problem page is the directly opened Playwright Backend Mocks HAR guide. Its Node backendMocks API is distinct from browser-context routeFromHAR.

observed.loopbackRoute: synthetic JSON returned through context-scoped fulfill route

fixture.scope: Exact bytes executed once by root. The fixture validates one native HTML5 list state and one loopback API mock only. It does not establish HAR behavior, generic widget support, or a blanket network guarantee.

execution.noTrafficMeasurement: No new analytics or private dashboard data was available in this content execution. Site visits, impressions, clicks, search volume, and mature cohort outcomes remain null; absence of access is not zero and is not a failed cohort.

modelRoles.policy: Actual model identifiers and token usage were not reported. No silent fallback or invented model use.

editorial.format: Five complete EN/ZH guides with direct answer, five topic-specific sections, worked or clearly hypothetical examples, at least three external links, three FAQs and natural series links.
editorial.sourceBoundary: Official current documentation is distinguished from vendor claims, publisher-reported experiences, dated issues, reviewer-opened pages and the exact root-executed synthetic fixture.
